claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureEquivalent
assumptions: Alphabet and Observation are supplied types; observe is a total deterministic function on all finite histories.
claims.statement: Two finite-list histories are future-equivalent exactly when every finite suffix yields equal task observations.
claims.ceiling: Definition over all finite list suffixes and the supplied observation function.
claims.residual: No application-specific task semantics, observation adequacy, or Myhill-Nerode minimality.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureEquivalent_refl
assumptions: Equality is the observation comparison.
claims.statement: Future-equivalence is reflexive for every supplied task observation.
claims.residual: No task source or utility result.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureEquivalent_symm
assumptions: Equality is symmetric.
claims.statement: Future-equivalence is symmetric for every supplied task observation.
claims.residual: No task source or utility result.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureEquivalent_trans
assumptions: Equality is transitive.
claims.statement: Future-equivalence is transitive for every supplied task observation.
claims.residual: No task source or utility result.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureEquivalent_right_congruent
assumptions: All finite lists are histories and all finite lists are admissible continuations; append associativity.
claims.statement: Equivalent histories remain equivalent after appending any common finite suffix.
claims.ceiling: Right congruence for the unrestricted list-history and all-suffix model.
claims.residual: The theorem does not apply unchanged to a restricted continuation aperture.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureSetoid
assumptions: The proved reflexive, symmetric, and transitive laws for future-equivalence.
claims.statement: Package future-equivalence as the Setoid relation used to form the history quotient.
claims.ceiling: A quotient relation for the declared task observation only.
claims.residual: No minimality or computational quotient representation.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.historyClass
assumptions: Histories are finite lists and the Setoid is future-equivalence for the supplied observation.
claims.statement: Map each history to its canonical class in the task-relative quotient.
claims.residual: No efficiency, canonical representative, or decidable equality claim.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.historyClass_eq_iff_futureEquivalent
assumptions: The quotient uses the declared future-equivalence Setoid.
claims.statement: Two histories have the same quotient class exactly when they are future-equivalent.
claims.ceiling: Standard quotient characterization for this Setoid.
claims.residual: No minimality theorem or computable representation.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureEquivalent_implies_current_observation
assumptions: The empty list is an admissible finite continuation.
claims.statement: Future-equivalent histories have equal current task observations, by taking the empty suffix.
claims.ceiling: A factorization prerequisite only; no totalization or reachable-image decoder theorem is claimed.
claims.residual: Decoder class, reachability, and task adequacy are not modeled.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.quotientObservation
assumptions: Observation is constant on each future-equivalence class, proved from the empty suffix.
claims.statement: The current task observation descends to a well-defined function on future-equivalence classes.
claims.residual: No decoder-class separation, reachable-image semantics, or computability.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.futureEquivalentOnAperture
assumptions: Aperture is a supplied predicate on allowed finite suffixes; observe remains total on all lists.
claims.statement: Restricted future-equivalence compares observations only for suffixes admitted by the supplied continuation aperture.
claims.residual: No history-indexed varying aperture or closure consequence without an explicit closure premise.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.apertureFutureEquivalent_right_congruent
assumptions: The continuation aperture is explicitly closed under prefixing the common appended task symbol.
claims.statement: Restricted future-equivalence is preserved by appending a task when every admitted suffix remains admitted after that task is prefixed.
claims.ceiling: Right congruence conditional on the displayed closure hypothesis.
claims.residual: Closure is not inferred for an arbitrary restricted aperture.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.constantTask
assumptions: Finite Boolean observation codomain.
claims.statement: A constant task observation returns false for every finite history.
claims.ceiling: Counterfixture to an unconditional nontrivial-usefulness claim.
claims.residual: No interpretation of a real task's usefulness.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.headTask
assumptions: Boolean alphabet and Option Bool observation.
claims.statement: A head-reading task observes the first Boolean symbol when present.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.constantTask_one_class
assumptions: Constant Boolean task observation.
claims.statement: Every pair of histories is future-equivalent under the constant task.
claims.residual: It does not establish nontrivial work or usefulness.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.constantTask_quotient_subsingleton
assumptions: The quotient is formed from the constant task's future-equivalence relation.
claims.statement: The constant task quotient has at most one class.
claims.residual: Usefulness, work, or adequacy remains unproved.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.headTask_distinguishes_histories
assumptions: The empty continuation is among all finite suffixes.
claims.statement: The head task distinguishes the empty history from the one-symbol false history.
claims.ceiling: A nontrivial task fixture; distinction follows already at the empty suffix.
claims.residual: No general nontriviality criterion for arbitrary tasks.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.task_mutation_changes_future_equivalence
assumptions: Compare the same two histories under the constant task and the head-reading task.
claims.statement: The same history pair is equivalent for the constant task but inequivalent for the head-reading task.
claims.ceiling: Finite fixture showing the quotient depends on the supplied task observation.
claims.residual: No source-versioning or task-selection authority claim.

claims.name: Experiments.Pal24HistoryQuotient.aperture_closure_is_load_bearing
assumptions: Boolean histories over finite lists.
Aperture admits exactly the empty suffix.
Observation is natural-number history length divided by two.
claims.statement: The aperture fails closure under prefixing false; empty and one-symbol histories agree within it, but after common extension [false], lengths one and two have different observations.
claims.ceiling: Finite counterfixture showing restricted right congruence can fail when the theorem’s continuation-closure premise is omitted.
claims.residual: This does not challenge all-finite-suffix right congruence or refute the source-scoped theorem; it demonstrates that arbitrary restricted apertures need not satisfy the premise.

manual_dispositions.detail: P0819 names a Myhill-Nerode realization but explicitly limits minimality to its theorem assumptions; this batch proves no minimality.
Reachable-image decoder variants, separately proved totalization, decoder-class separation, aperture stability across task changes, and forget-to-A8 remain outside this model.
